chapter_theme: Kuruntokai 361-380: the friend at work, mocking the diviner (362), dissuading departure (363), urging marriage through tears, gossip and a broken promise (365, 372, 379), and reporting the asking (374); girls who love beyond union (361, 371, 377); courtesans and a forbearing wife in the watered town (364, 368, 370); elopement seen by friend and foster mother (369, 378); waiting through the rains (367, 380); and the man's praise of a beloved warm in winter and cool in summer (376).

361.reading: The girl tells her friend that her mother is worth more than the high world itself, for she did not forbid her to clasp, crushing its soft leaves, the whole kaanthal plant that the flood of the evening rain on his hill brought down in the morning, nor to carry it home and plant it.
361.nuance: The mother's not forbidding is praised as above heaven because she does not know what the plant is: the girl embraces the hill of her lover in a flower the flood carried, and the mother's innocence is the girl's whole freedom.

thinai_evidence.note: a kaanthal from the lover's hill is the token of the poem

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; she opens with அம்ம வாழி தோழி

362.reading: The friend asks the old-mouthed diviner who came rejoicing in Murugan's rite to hold back his anger and answer one question: if he kills a small kid, offers rice-balls of many colours, strokes the girl's fragrant brow and makes his worship, will the bright-garlanded chest of the man of the sky-touching hill who afflicted her also eat the offering?
362.nuance: அணங்கிய names the man as the possessing power the rite blames on the god, so the question to the velan reveals the secret (அறத்தொடு நிற்றல்) while seeming only to mock the rite.

thinai_evidence.note: the possession rite of Murugan belongs to the hill

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; she addresses the velan (வேல) directly; the mother is the real hearer

363.reading: The friend asks the man whether it is sweet to cross the cruel hard waste, leaving his sweet companion, where the fine bull with garland-ringed horns chews the long-eared red-stemmed grass and, looking at his soft-eyed doe, suffers the heat and rests with her in the thin striped shade of the hollow-trunked ukaay.

thinai_evidence.note: the friend tries to stop his going across the waste

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; பெரும is the man about to leave

iraicchi.act: the bull stays by its doe in the scorching land and shares the thin shade with her
iraicchi.sense: even the beast of the waste keeps beside its mate in hardship, so the man should not leave his

364.reading: The household concubine says that the proud wife of the man of the town where the otter among the tangled cane gets a vaalai fish for its daily food speaks behind her back, they say; well, the days of the thunangai dance of the bright-bangled women have come, and there, when eyes clash, comes the contest of young men eager to take brides.
364.nuance: The otter that takes a vaalai every day is the traditional figure for the husband enjoying her without effort, but the poem names no situation it maps onto (the anchor is the wife's slander, not his pleasure), so it stays scene; the concubine answers the slander by a public challenge at the festival, not by denial.

thinai_evidence.note: the rivalry of wife and concubine in the man of the watered town

comparisons.tenor: the women's shoulders, rounded like bamboo

thurai_akam.speaker: parathai
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; she answers the wife's talk to those who carried it, so the wife's people

365.reading: The friend tells the man of the land of great rocks, where the waterfall brimming on the tall peak no one can approach sounds like a cool drum beside the jackfruit trees, that the eyes of the girl he loves weep every day and never stop dripping while her shining conch bangles slip.
365.nuance: The falls that sound like a drum in his own land hint at the wedding drum he has not yet sounded; that is a single match of mood, not two pairs, so it is left as a simile.

thinai_evidence.note: peak, waterfall and jackfruit are the hill

comparisons.vehicle: ததும்பிய அருவி தண்ணென் முழவின் இமிழிசை காட்டும்

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; நாட and நீ நயந்தோள் address the man

366.reading: The friend says that, beyond what destiny has fixed and arranged, who are we to measure the man's worth; when I spoke otherwise the girl would not accept it, and looking at the wide-petalled blue lily that has burst open in the green-eyed dark pool, her eyes ripened with tears: this jewelled girl's resolve is not false.
366.nuance: பால் is the destiny that pairs lovers; the friend argues that the choice is not hers to judge, and the girl's tears at a flower like her own eyes are offered as proof. Lines 5 and 6 (உள்ளகை பழுத கண்ணள்) are hard to construe.

thinai_evidence.note: the mountain pool and its lily are the hill

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; she defends the girl's choice, most likely to the mother or foster mother

367.reading: The friend tells the girl that even if the cruel man shows no grace, her bangled shoulders may regain their beauty: look there, now that the dense dark rain has begun, his hill has come into view in his land, its cool fragrant boulders shining like a washed gem in the falls down which the noisy troop of girls slides with delight.
367.nuance: The sight of his hill is offered as a cure in itself: the friend does not promise he will come, only that seeing his land washed by the first rains will restore her.

thinai_evidence.note: she is comforted as the rains begin and he has not come

comparisons.tenor: the rain-washed rocks of his hill

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; நின் தோள் and உவக்காண் தோழி address the girl

368.reading: The wife tells her gentle friend, three times over, that she can only bear with strength the shame of a dark beauty that has lost its good modesty, and cannot say it aloud; for the sake of the town where small and great live, let them embrace him often in a blameless state, like the great tree on the firm bank of a flood that never fails.
368.nuance: The riverbank tree is the town's common shade, standing in a flood that comes every day: her quarrel would be a public loss, so she makes endurance a civic duty. Lines 2 and 3 are obscure, and the sense of நன்னாண் நீத்த is not certain.

thinai_evidence.note: the wife chooses to receive the straying husband for the town's sake

comparisons.vehicle: நாளிடைப் படாஅ நளிநீர் நீத்தத் திண்கரைப் பெருமரம் போலத்
comparisons.tenor: the household that stands firm and shelters the town

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; மெல்லியலோயே is the friend who urges her to refuse him

369.reading: The friend tells the girl that their man has granted it: let us go through the forest of the waste, where the west wind swings the dense white pods of the vaakai and their seeds rattle like the pebbles of an anklet.
369.nuance: The anklet's rattle in the dry pods is a wedding sound heard in the waste: the friend makes the dreaded road ring like the girl's own feet.

thinai_evidence.note: the wasteland with its summer wind

comparisons.tenor: the rattling seeds of the vaakai pods

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; செல்வாம் தோழி invites the girl to go

370.reading: The courtesan says that with the man of the cool ford, where bees open the beautiful plump bud of the water-lily in the pond, when they sit they are two side by side, when they lie they fit together like fingers round a bow, and when he goes to his good home they are one, left on one side.

thinai_evidence.note: pond, water-lily and ford are the watered land

thurai_akam.speaker: parathai
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; she speaks of the man to her own company, likely within the wife's hearing

ullurai.tenor: the man who opens a young woman's love and moves on

pairs.situation: the man takes her first love
she, young and unopened, is the bud
he is of the ford town and goes back to his house

ullurai.speaker_fit: the courtesan, as 'anyone else', may use the pond of the marutham town freely (porul 7.29)

371.reading: The girl tells her friend that though she has not joined the man of the land where hill rice sown on the cloud-dark slope is ripened by the waterfall, her bangles slip and pallor spreads over her body: that love is great indeed.
371.nuance: மருவேன் makes the paradox: the signs of a love affair without its embrace. The hill rice needs no irrigation, as her love needs no meeting.

thinai_evidence.note: hill rice watered by falls is kurinji

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; தோழி in line 4

ullurai.tenor: the love he sowed, which grows of itself without his tending

pairs.situation: it ripens of itself without his care or union
it grows on her, unseen and unwatered by him

ullurai.speaker_fit: the girl uses hill rice of her own hill country, a thing she knows (porul 7.26)

372.reading: The friend says that in this town of passers-by gossip rose before the mound on the sand ridge could dry, a heap the sea threw up with flowing mud where the fierce wind piles long white dunes that bury the palmyras' crowns, their saw-edged fronds and shoots, in the shore grove where crested heaps bow.
372.nuance: The wind piling sand over the palms looks like a figure of gossip burying the lovers, but the poem gives no pairs beyond the swiftness, so it is scene; the shore that keeps reshaping itself is the measure of how fast talk moves.

thinai_evidence.note: the sea shore and its sand ridges

comparisons.vehicle: புலர்பதங் கொள்ளா வளவை அலரெழுந் தன்றிவ் வழங்க லூரே

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; news of gossip is told to hasten marriage, so most likely to the man

373.reading: The friend asks what harm can come, even if the earth shifts its place, water and fire change natures and the great sea of bright waves shows a shore, from fear of the hot-mouthed women's gossip to their bond with the man of the high hill, where the long-haired, sharp-toothed, black-fingered male langur beats the flower-scented jackfruit until it perfumes the kaanthal-fenced hamlet.
373.nuance: The jackfruit's scent filling the hamlet after the langur beats it is a near miss for ullurai (the affair spreading through the village), but only one pair holds; the adynata of earth, fire, water and sea are the poem's own claim.

thinai_evidence.note: the langur and jackfruit of the hill

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; தோழி in line 4 is the girl

374.reading: The friend says that after she made father and mother understand and spoke out the hidden matter, the man of the hill came and asked for the girl, and in his good resolve it was all agreed; the town, deluded, is more tangled than the nests the curved-backed weaver birds hang from the tall dark palmyra.
374.nuance: The weaver's nest is a marvel of order that looks like chaos; the town that misread the secret is more tangled still, now that the truth has ended in a proper asking.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill lord asks for her hand after the secret is told

comparisons.vehicle: தூங்கணங் குரீஇ நீடிரும் பெண்ணைத் தொடுத்த கூடினும் மயங்கிய

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; she reports the outcome, most likely to the girl or to the man

375.reading: The friend says it is good if he does not come today, for on the wide dark field of the slope where the small millet has ripened, if the striped one comes by night, the watchmen's small thondakam drum sounds even at midnight, since the night guards never sleep.
375.nuance: Wishing him away is the friend's way of naming the dangers he braves; the drum guards the millet against the tiger and so guards the girl against him too.

thinai_evidence.note: millet field, hill drum and slope

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; அம்ம வாழி தோழி; the man is likely meant to overhear

376.reading: The man says that in summer she is cool like the sandal of the dread slopes of Pothiyil, hard to reach and unknown to living men, and in the cold season she is a little warm like the heart of a lotus that closed softly, holding the swaying sunlight, when the sun gathered its bent rays.
376.nuance: She is a counter-climate: the lotus that shuts at sunset keeps the day's warmth inside, as she keeps warmth for the cold months.

thinai_evidence.note: the man's delight in her body is the union of kurinji

comparisons.tenor: her warmth in the cold season

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; he speaks of her in the third person

377.reading: The girl tells her friend that the beauty of her flower-like kohl-lined eyes is gone and, on top of that, her soft shoulders fair as bangles have grown thin, and there is no undoing the small good friendship she made with the man of a land beyond knowing.
377.nuance: சிறுநன் னட்பு is bitter: a small, good friendship has cost her eyes and shoulders. Line 1 is supplied from another text and line 3 (தோழியாற் றலையே) is hard to divide.

thinai_evidence.note: the man of the hill country; little else fixes the land

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; தோழி in line 3

378.reading: The foster mother prays that the sun may not burn on the waste the young girl crossed, leaving us, with the youth of the bright-pointed long spear; may it be tree-shade, may the small path at the foot of the hill be thick with sand, and may cool clouds hang over it.
378.nuance: Each wish undoes one property of paalai (sun, shadeless path, burning ground, cloudless sky), so the blessing is a description of the waste in the negative.

thinai_evidence.note: the wasteland of the elopement, wished cool

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; a blessing spoken to no one in the poem, perhaps to the gods of the road

379.reading: The friend asks where he is today, the man of the land where the hunter digging an old pit on the hill finds, with the tubers, a wide-faced pure gem: he who stroked your thick hair and said 'girl of close bangles, when your understanding ripens, you will come into our house.'
379.nuance: The promise was conditional on her growing up (அறிவுகாழ்க் கொள்ளும் அளவை); the friend's 'where is he today' turns the image against him: he found the gem and has not taken it home.

thinai_evidence.note: hill, hunter and wild tuber

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; தோழி and நீ address the girl

ullurai.tenor: the man who sought a pleasure and found a wife

pairs.situation: the man who came for a passing love
he gains the girl, a treasure worth taking home

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses a hunter of the hill in a kurinji poem, without leaving its land (porul 7.27)

380.reading: The friend says the sky, spreading to blind the heavens and roaring many times like the drums kings beat in victory, does not stop raining; our lover is in a land very far off, not before us; how shall we bear it, friend, now that the soft-tufted eengai flowers fall and the cold harsh days stand before us?
380.nuance: The season of his promised return has not only come but is passing into the cold; the cloud sounds like a king's victory drum, a reminder of what keeps men away.

thinai_evidence.note: the rains and then the cold arrive while she waits

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred: the colophon gives only the speaker; யாங்குச்செய் வாங்கொல் தோழி; the speaker shares the grief

links.note: In Akananuru 98 the girl tells her friend that the mother does not know her ache is eased only on the hill lord's chest, while the velan's rite goes on; in Kuruntokai 362 the friend puts that same claim to the velan as a question: will his chest eat the offering?
links.teaches: The pair shows the step from private knowledge to disclosure: what the girl can only say to her friend in the long poem, the friend turns into a riddle spoken at the rite itself, so the mockery of the diviner is the means by which the secret reaches the mother.

links.note: Kural 1151's friend refuses comfort with an ultimatum about who will still be alive when he returns; Kuruntokai 363's friend asks whether crossing the waste is sweet when even the bull there stays by its doe.
links.teaches: The same dissuasion of a man about to leave is made by threat in the couplet and by the example of the road's own creatures in the poem, so the pair shows the friend has two arguments, death of the one left and the shame of being less faithful than a beast.

links.note: Both are courtesans answering, within hearing of the wife's side, the wife's talk against them: in Akananuru 76 she vows to hold him as the Kaveri took Atti; in Kuruntokai 364 she points to the coming thunangai festival where eyes clash.
links.teaches: Held together, the two poems show the concubine's convention of answering slander not with denial but with a public contest announced in advance, a river's seizure or a festival's rivalry, so the household quarrel is moved out into the town's open spaces.

links.note: In Kuruntokai 229 onlookers see destiny (பால்) at work in two who fought as children and are now joined; in 366 the friend invokes the same destiny before any outcome to refuse to judge the man.
links.teaches: Destiny serves after the fact as the onlookers' explanation and before the fact as the friend's argument for consent, so the pair shows the akam idea of பால் doing persuasive work, not only describing what happened.

links.note: In 369 the friend calls the paalai road pleasant, its pods rattling like anklets, and urges the girl to go; in 378 the foster mother, after the girl has gone, can only pray that the same road's sun and bare paths be cooled.
links.teaches: The one elopement road is a promise to the girl's accomplice and a danger to the woman who raised her, so the pair shows the akam books dividing a single event between voices who cannot both be right about the land.

links.note: Purananuru 3 tells the Pandya that even if the earth shifts his word must not; Kuruntokai 373's friend says that even if the earth shifts and fire and water change places, the lovers' bond suffers no harm from gossip.
links.teaches: The akam friend borrows the puram formula for a king's unbreakable word and gives it to a secret love, so the pair shows that the lovers' bond was claimed in the language of royal oath, and that a pledge, not a feeling, is what kalavu asks to be trusted.

links.note: In Akananuru 122 the girl lists the town, mother, guards, dogs, moon and owl that keep watch, and complains that when all sleep he does not come; in Kuruntokai 375 the friend says it is better he does not come, since the guards beat their drum all night against the tiger.
links.teaches: The same sleepless watch is used to reproach the lover for missing his chance and to wish him away from it, so the pair shows that the catalogue of obstacles is addressed to the man in both directions, and that its real end is to make the night visit impossible and marriage necessary.

links.note: Kural 1104's man asks where she found a fire that burns when he moves away and cools when he draws near; Kuruntokai 376's man says she is cool in summer and warm in the cold season.
links.teaches: Both men praise her as a reversal of temperature, but the couplet makes it depend on his distance and the poem on the season, so together they show the convention of the beloved as a climate of her own, which the Kural turns inward into the lover's desire.

links.note: In Akananuru 283 the friend, arranging the elopement, wishes rain to fall on the forest and cool it so the road is sweet; in Kuruntokai 378 the foster mother, after the girl has gone, prays the sun not burn and cool clouds hang over the waste.
links.teaches: The same wish for a cooled desert passes from the accomplice who sends the girl to the woman who has lost her, so the pair shows the foster mother's grief taking the form of blessing, joining in the elopement she did not choose.

links.note: In Akananuru 84 the man in the king's war camp sees the drum-voiced rain-clouds and thinks of his wife in her small village; in Kuruntokai 380 the waiting women hear the cloud roar like the drums kings beat in victory while the lover stays far away.
links.teaches: Read together, the simile in the women's mouth names the cause the man's poem shows from inside, the king's campaign, so the rains are the same drum to both and the season of war and the season of waiting are one.

source_issues: Kuruntokai colophons give only the speaker (தோழி கூற்று and the like), so every addressee and stage in thurai_akam is inferred from the poem; each item says so in its note.
372 line 1 carries a stray comma inside a line (பனைத்தலைக், கருக்குடை); the sense of lines 1 to 5 is hard to fix.
377 line 1 is missing from the base text and is supplied from sangamtamil.com; line 3 (தோழியாற் றலையே) is hard to divide.
375 and 379 have no poet in the colophon.
363, 365, 366 and 378 each have one line repaired from tamilvu; 374 line 2 was a TSCII leftover (தௌிய) repaired to தெளிய; the repairs read correctly.

Thinai differs from the colophon in 367 (mullai: the first rains and waiting, not marutham), 376 (kurinji: the man's delight in her body, with Pothiyil sandal; the colophon says neythal) and 380 (mullai: waiting through the rains into the cold; the colophon says paalai).
